text: what does error QRV-4012 mean
design_note: Exact rare token (error code). Embeddings treat QRV-4012 as noise; BM25 should nail it. The index page lists the code with a one-liner: partial credit, and a lexical near-trap above the real entry.

text: flush_interval_ms default
design_note: Exact parameter name with no natural-language context. Vector search has almost nothing to embed; the API reference is the only doc naming it.

text: checkpoint_store_uri setting
design_note: Exact config key. The yaml reference defines it (2); the checkpointing guide mentions it in passing (1).

text: my pipeline produces data faster than the database can accept and memory keeps growing
design_note: Describes backpressure without using 'backpressure', 'flow', 'buffer', or 'stage'. BM25 has nothing rare to grip; the embedding must carry it.

text: guarantee each record is applied a single time even if the runner crashes mid-way
design_note: Paraphrase of effectively-once delivery; shares almost no tokens with the target's own terms. Checkpointing explains the recovery mechanism but not the guarantee: partial.

text: where do records end up when they fail over and over
design_note: Paraphrase of dead-letter routing avoiding 'dead', 'letter', 'queue', 'retry'. The retry guide mentions the hand-off once: partial.

text: set up OAuth authentication for a pipeline
design_note: The changelog says 'OAuth' seven times and answers nothing; the guide says it twice and answers everything. Token-frequency ranking takes the bait.

text: configure retry behavior for transient failures
design_note: The API index is dense with retry-named symbols and explains none of them. BM25 favors it; the guide is the answer.

text: enable schema validation on a source
design_note: The FAQ repeats the phrase 'schema validation' in five question titles and answers none of them. The guide answers in its first sentence.

text: authenticate a connector with an API key
design_note: OAuth guide is the semantic sibling (both 'authentication'); embeddings pull it in, but it does not answer the API-key question. Graded 0 by design.

text: increase pipeline throughput by tuning batch size
design_note: Rate-limits is the sibling: semantically 'about limits on speed' but it concerns the REST endpoint cap, not batch tuning. Graded 0.

text: write pipeline output to an S3 bucket
design_note: Directional confusion: source vs sink for the same backend. Embeddings see near-identical text; only the direction differs. Source graded 0.

text: how do I start a pipeline in Quorva v1
design_note: Version-pinned ask. The v2 page is right topic, wrong version (1); migration shows both (1). Retrievers that ignore the version token rank v2 first.

text: qv.execute() arguments in v2
design_note: Pinned to v2 by symbol and by word. The v1 page documents a different API entirely: graded 0. Migration maps the arguments: partial.

text: migrate run() calls from v1 to v2
design_note: The migration page is the only one that maps old names to new. Each version's own page covers one side: partial each.

text: configure the DLQ
design_note: The dead-letter guide never uses the acronym; only the glossary bridges DLQ to dead-letter queue. Lexical match fails; embeddings may or may not bridge it.

text: does Quorva support exactly-once processing
design_note: The docs' term is 'effectively-once'; the community's is 'exactly-once'. Zero lexical overlap on the term that matters.

text: what is the QPS limit on the ingest API
design_note: Docs say 'requests per second'; the query says QPS. The glossary defines the acronym: partial credit and the only lexical bridge.

text: run a pipeline without checkpointing
design_note: 'Without X' where the X guide is the strongest match on both signals. The checkpointing guide names the key but not how to turn it off: partial.

text: authenticate without storing secrets in the config file
design_note: Both auth guides show config-file credentials and match 'authenticate' strongly; both graded 0. Only the environment/workload-identity page satisfies the constraint.

text: deploy a pipeline without using the CLI
design_note: The CLI deploy page is the lexical and semantic magnet for 'deploy'; the constraint excludes it. Graded 0 by design.

text: QRV-5002 checkpoint corrupt
design_note: Exact error code with no natural-language context; embeddings treat QRV-5002 as noise. The index page lists it with a one-liner (partial); the dedicated page answers it.

text: batch_rows argument on PostgresSink
design_note: Exact parameter + symbol name. Only the API reference names batch_rows; nothing to embed semantically.

text: commit_interval_s default
design_note: Exact config key whose default (30) is stated in the checkpointing guide (2); the yaml reference lists the key (1).

text: qv.execute limit argument
design_note: Exact v2 symbol + argument. The v2 page is the only doc naming qv.execute's limit; v1 uses max_records, so it must not win.

text: dead_letter_uri key
design_note: Exact config key; the DLQ guide defines it (2), the yaml reference lists it (1).

text: will records come out in the same sequence they went in
design_note: Paraphrase of ordering guarantees; avoids 'order', 'partition', 'sequence'-as-noun. Minimal lexical overlap with the target.

text: avoid reprocessing everything from the start after a crash
design_note: Describes checkpoint resume without 'checkpoint', 'offset', 'resume'. Delivery guide covers the recovery it enables (partial).

text: spread one slow step across more cpu cores
design_note: Paraphrase of parallelism/workers avoiding those words. Performance page touches scaling (partial).

text: stop one slow stage from eating all the memory
design_note: Second backpressure angle, different wording from q-par-1; still avoids 'backpressure'/'buffer'.

text: make applying the same write twice harmless
design_note: Paraphrase of idempotency avoiding the word. Delivery guide leans on it (partial).

text: change the batch size to improve Postgres write throughput
design_note: qrv-tuning-faq covers 'batch size', 'Postgres', 'write throughput', 'improve' across unanswered questions; the API reference answers using 'batch_rows'/'flush' and fewer query words. Distinct-term coverage should rank the FAQ first on BM25.

text: retry a failed webhook delivery with backoff
design_note: qrv-webhook-changelog hits retry/failed/webhook/delivery/backoff every line; the retry guide explains backoff with other words. Coverage trap.

text: validate the pipeline configuration before deploying
design_note: qrv-deploy-faq saturates validate/pipeline/configuration/deploy; qrv-cli-validate is the actual answer. Coverage trap.

text: set the commit interval for checkpoint state
design_note: qrv-config-index lists commit/interval/checkpoint/state as bare keys; the checkpointing guide answers (2), yaml reference lists the key (1).

text: authenticate the webhook sink with an API key
design_note: qrv-auth-faq repeats authenticate/webhook/sink/API/key across unanswered Qs; the api-key guide is the real answer. Coverage trap.

text: bring changes from a Postgres database into the pipeline
design_note: Near-sibling qrv-sink-postgres (writes TO postgres) is the embedding magnet and shares 'Postgres'/'sink' tokens; the query is about reading FROM. Sink graded 0 by omission; direction is the whole trap.

text: cap how many records a single run will process
design_note: Sibling qrv-guide-rate-limits ('limit' on the API) is semantically adjacent; the answer is qv.execute's limit argument. Rate-limits graded 0.

text: watch per-stage record counts and timings while it runs
design_note: Sibling qrv-cli-status (also 'while it runs', reports health) is the magnet; metrics endpoint is the answer. Status graded 0 -- it reports control-plane state, not per-stage counts.

text: sign requests with a credential that expires and refreshes
design_note: Sibling qrv-auth-apikey (keys do NOT expire) shares 'credential'/'auth' space; only OAuth (tokens expire/refresh) fits. API-key graded 0.

text: the fastest file source for columnar typed data
design_note: Siblings qrv-source-csv / qrv-source-jsonl are file sources too (embedding-close); only Parquet is columnar. Others graded 0 by omission.

text: add a sink in Quorva v1
design_note: v1-pinned. The v2 .to() page is right topic wrong version (1); migration maps them (1). Retrievers ignoring the version token rank v2 first.

text: the .to() operator for attaching sinks in v2
design_note: v2-pinned by exact operator; v1 add_sink page is a different API, graded 0. Migration maps (1).

text: blocking argument to run() in v1
design_note: v1 symbol (blocking, run()). v2 uses wait on qv.execute, so the v2 page must not win. Migration maps (1).

text: what replaced max_records in v2
design_note: Only the migration page maps old->new (max_records -> limit); each version page covers one side (partial).

text: state_uri versus state_dir
design_note: The rename is documented only on the migration page (2); v2 page names state_uri (1).

text: set up a CDC source
design_note: Docs say 'change data capture' / 'logical-replication slot', never 'CDC'. Only the extended glossary bridges the acronym (1); the Postgres source is the answer (2).

text: tail latency of sink writes
design_note: Docs say 'p99 write latency'; query says 'tail latency'. Glossary-ext defines the synonym (1); batching guide is the answer (2).

text: does it support 2PC for sink writes
design_note: Delivery guide says 'two-phase commit', never '2PC'. Glossary-ext bridges (1).

text: RPS ceiling on the ingest API
design_note: Docs say 'requests per second'; query says RPS. Both glossaries bridge (1); rate-limits answers (2).

text: at-least-once versus exactly-once delivery
design_note: Docs' term is 'effectively-once'; query uses the industry pair. Zero overlap on the decisive term.

text: run a pipeline without deploying it to a fleet
design_note: qrv-cli-deploy and qrv-deployment-overview are the lexical+semantic magnets for 'pipeline'/'fleet'; the constraint excludes them. Local run is the answer; deploy pages graded 0.

text: read a source without tracking offsets or resuming
design_note: Checkpointing/offset docs are the strong match on both signals; the constraint wants state off. Ephemeral is the answer; checkpointing names the knob (1).

text: let a bad record through without failing its batch
design_note: Schema-enforce docs match 'record'/'batch'/'fail' strongly; the constraint wants the non-failing path -- warn mode, in the schema guide.

text: run without persisting any pipeline state
design_note: Second ephemeral angle; checkpointing is the magnet, the constraint excludes it (named partial).

text: supply credentials without environment variables, from a file
design_note: qrv-auth-env (environment credentials) is the magnet and the excluded path; the file-based api-key guide satisfies the constraint (2). Env page named partial because it's the contrast, not graded 0, to keep the trap honest.

text: across local, fleet, and ephemeral modes, what checkpoint interval applies
design_note: Support set: the three mode docs — qrv-runner-embedded (local), qrv-runner-fleet, qrv-runner-ephemeral. The local runner uses the pipeline default (30 s), fleet overrides it (10 s), and ephemeral has no checkpoint interval; each value lives in a different document, so one chunk cannot answer it.

text: what happens to unfinished work after a failure in each execution mode
design_note: Support set: qrv-runner-embedded, qrv-runner-fleet, qrv-runner-ephemeral. Three different behaviours (retry in place, reassign and execute twice, restart from source offsets); the comparison needs all three.

text: what is the maximum number of in-flight batches in each execution mode (local, fleet, ephemeral)
design_note: Support set: qrv-runner-embedded, qrv-runner-fleet, qrv-runner-ephemeral. Values are 8, 64 per worker, and 4; lexical overlap is high, so retrieval must return all three rather than the best-matching one.

text: what memory ceiling does each execution mode enforce (local, fleet, ephemeral)
design_note: Support set: qrv-runner-embedded, qrv-runner-fleet, qrv-runner-ephemeral. 512 MiB, 2 GiB per worker, and 256 MiB. Units differ, so the answer is only complete with every member.

text: what is the p95 latency SLA for each region
design_note: Support set: qrv-region-eu, qrv-region-us, qrv-region-ap, qrv-region-jp. Four distinct values (120/80/180/150 ms), four documents; missing any region is an incomplete answer.

text: how long does each region retain stored records by default
design_note: Support set: qrv-region-eu, qrv-region-us, qrv-region-ap, qrv-region-jp. Two regions retain 30 days and two 45 days; the grouping is only visible with the whole set.

text: which regions require in-region data residency
design_note: Support set: qrv-region-eu, qrv-region-us, qrv-region-ap, qrv-region-jp. Every region pins data in-region, so the correct answer is the full set and a partial retrieval under-answers.

text: what are the regional edge endpoints
design_note: Support set: qrv-region-eu, qrv-region-us, qrv-region-ap, qrv-region-jp. Each doc names one quorva-edge-* endpoint; the identifiers are lexically similar, which stresses returning all four.

text: what access token lifetime applies to mTLS, workload identity and OIDC
design_note: Support set: qrv-auth-mtls, qrv-auth-workload, qrv-auth-oidc. Scoped to the three documented service methods because the older auth docs (qrv-auth-apikey, qrv-auth-oauth) describe different credential models and are not part of this comparison. Lifetimes are 15 minutes, 1 hour, and 10 minutes within this scoped set; qrv-auth-oauth, outside the scope, also states one hour.

text: which of mTLS, workload identity and OIDC rotates credentials automatically
design_note: Support set: qrv-auth-mtls, qrv-auth-workload, qrv-auth-oidc. Scope is explicit; the three rotation descriptions are spread across the docs.

text: what audit identifier is recorded for each of the mTLS, workload identity and OIDC methods
design_note: Support set: qrv-auth-mtls, qrv-auth-workload, qrv-auth-oidc. Three exact tokens (peer_serial, spiffe_id, sub) in three documents.

text: how do mTLS, workload identity and OIDC authenticate a caller
design_note: Support set: qrv-auth-mtls, qrv-auth-workload, qrv-auth-oidc. Three different mechanisms; the scope is explicit so the older API-key and OAuth docs are out of scope.

text: what transport delivery guarantee does each streaming sink document
design_note: Support set: qrv-sink-kafka, qrv-sink-kinesis, qrv-sink-pubsub. All three document at-least-once transports, with Pub/Sub adding a conditional exactly-once subscription option; completeness is the point.

text: what maximum message size does each streaming sink accept
design_note: Support set: qrv-sink-kafka, qrv-sink-kinesis, qrv-sink-pubsub. 1 MiB, 1 MiB, and 10 MiB; two values repeat, so full support is the discriminating metric.

text: how is ordering preserved in each streaming sink
design_note: Support set: qrv-sink-kafka, qrv-sink-kinesis, qrv-sink-pubsub. Per partition, per shard, and by ordering key; three different phrasings.

text: how long does each streaming sink retain messages by default
design_note: Support set: qrv-sink-kafka, qrv-sink-kinesis, qrv-sink-pubsub. Kafka defers retention to the broker, Kinesis 24 hours, Pub/Sub 7 days; one member has no sink-side default, which only a full retrieval reveals.

text: what is the RunnerLease renewal period and why did fleet pipelines stall in February 2026
design_note: Joining entity: RunnerLease. The fleet doc supplies the 5-second renewal period; the postmortem supplies the coordinator bug, and the postmortem deliberately does not restate the period. Required documents: qrv-runner-fleet and qrv-incident-2026-02-lease.

text: how often does RunnerLease renew and what did the fix after the February incident change
design_note: Joining entity: RunnerLease. The renewal period is in qrv-runner-fleet; the serialisation fix is in qrv-incident-2026-02-lease. Neither document states the other's half.

text: which regional endpoint serves eu-west-1 and what caused its May 2026 outage
design_note: Joining entity: quorva-edge-eu. The endpoint-to-region mapping is only in qrv-region-eu; the cause (expired certificate) only in qrv-incident-2026-05-eu. Required documents: qrv-region-eu and qrv-incident-2026-05-eu.

text: what is the eu-west-1 p95 latency SLA and why did its edge endpoint stop accepting connections
design_note: Joining entity: quorva-edge-eu. SLA only in qrv-region-eu; the TLS failure only in qrv-incident-2026-05-eu.

text: how do mTLS clients prove their identity to CertificateAuthority and what does the upcoming intermediate rotation require
design_note: Joining entity: CertificateAuthority. The presentation of a CA-issued certificate is only in qrv-auth-mtls; the rotation requirement is only in qrv-security-advisory-ca, which states no client-authentication mechanism. Required documents: qrv-auth-mtls and qrv-security-advisory-ca.

text: how often do mTLS client certificates rotate and what changes when the CertificateAuthority intermediate rotates
design_note: Joining entity: CertificateAuthority. The 24-hour certificate lifetime is only in qrv-auth-mtls; the advisory states that client certificates are unaffected and a new intermediate must be trusted.

text: what transport guarantee does the Kafka sink document and why did a rebalance produce duplicates in July 2026
design_note: Joining entity: KafkaPublisher. The guarantee is in qrv-sink-kafka; the retry-after-rebalance cause is in qrv-incident-2026-07-kafka, which refers to the contract rather than restating it.

text: what is KafkaPublisher's maximum message size and did the July 2026 duplicates lose records
design_note: Joining entity: KafkaPublisher. The maximum message size is only in qrv-sink-kafka; the record-loss conclusion is only in qrv-incident-2026-07-kafka. Each document supplies a different fact. Required documents: qrv-sink-kafka and qrv-incident-2026-07-kafka.

text: which mode does quorva replay run in and what does that mode do with checkpoints
design_note: Joining entity: EphemeralMode. Replay names the mode but not its checkpoint behaviour; qrv-runner-ephemeral defines the behaviour but not replay. This is the pure join: mode plus property.

text: what memory ceiling applies to a quorva replay run
design_note: Joining entity: EphemeralMode. Only qrv-cli-replay says replay runs in EphemeralMode; only qrv-runner-ephemeral states that mode's 256 MiB ceiling. Neither alone answers.

text: how many availability zones does the region behind quorva-edge-ap use and why did the September failover add latency
design_note: Joining entity: quorva-edge-ap. The zone count is only in qrv-region-ap; the cross-region failover cost is only in qrv-incident-2026-09-ap. Required documents: qrv-region-ap and qrv-incident-2026-09-ap.

text: what is the APAC region p95 latency SLA and what did p95 reach during the September breach
design_note: Joining entity: quorva-edge-ap. SLA in qrv-region-ap; the 310 ms breach figure in qrv-incident-2026-09-ap, which no longer restates the SLA.

text: which component brokers OIDC authorization codes and why did logins fail in October 2026
design_note: Joining entity: OidcBroker. The brokering role is in qrv-auth-oidc; the clock-skew cause is in qrv-incident-2026-10-oidc.

text: what is the OIDC access token lifetime and what did the October postmortem rule out as the cause
design_note: Joining entity: OidcBroker. The lifetime is only in qrv-auth-oidc; the postmortem says the lifetime was not the issue without stating it.

text: what assignment rule does EmbeddedScheduler follow and how does a short checkpoint interval affect throughput
design_note: Joining entity: EmbeddedScheduler. The oldest-first, no-preemption rule is in qrv-runner-embedded; the checkpoint-pause interaction is in qrv-tuning-scheduler.

text: what is the local runner default checkpoint interval and how does the scheduler interact with it
design_note: Joining entity: EmbeddedScheduler. The 30-second default is in qrv-runner-embedded; the interaction is in qrv-tuning-scheduler, which no longer restates the default.

text: what is the default watermark delay and why did the April 2026 pipeline lose records
design_note: Joining entity: WatermarkTracker. The guide supplies the default delay; the postmortem supplies the loss cause (an unconsumed late-data side output), and neither document restates the other's half. Required documents: qrv-guide-watermarks and qrv-incident-2026-04-watermark.

text: how often is the watermark_lag gauge emitted and what fixed the April 2026 late-data loss
design_note: Joining entity: WatermarkTracker. The guide supplies the lag-report cadence; the postmortem supplies the fix, and neither document restates the other's half. Required documents: qrv-guide-watermarks and qrv-incident-2026-04-watermark.

text: how often does the secret rotation job re-read the credential file and why did the January 2026 pipeline keep using an expired credential
design_note: Joining entity: SecretRotationJob. The guide supplies the poll interval; the postmortem supplies why the swap never happened, and neither document restates the other's half. Required documents: qrv-guide-secret-rotation and qrv-incident-2026-01-secret.

text: when does a rotated secret take effect and what warning was added after the January 2026 credential expiry
design_note: Joining entity: SecretRotationJob. The guide supplies the timing (a swap is noticed on the 15-minute re-read) and its scope; the postmortem supplies the added warning, and neither document restates the other's half. Required documents: qrv-guide-secret-rotation and qrv-incident-2026-01-secret.

text: how long are CDC replication slots retained and why did the June 2026 pipelines take a full snapshot
design_note: Joining entity: PostgresSource. The guide supplies the retention window; the postmortem supplies how it was exceeded, and neither document restates the other's half. Required documents: qrv-guide-cdc-retention and qrv-incident-2026-06-cdc.

text: when does the CDC acknowledgement position advance and what guard was added after June 2026
design_note: Joining entity: PostgresSource. The guide supplies the ack cadence; the postmortem supplies the pause guard, and neither document restates the other's half. Required documents: qrv-guide-cdc-retention and qrv-incident-2026-06-cdc.

text: what compression codec is the default and why did sink workers in August 2026 saturate their CPU
design_note: Joining entity: CodecNegotiator. The guide supplies the default codec; the postmortem supplies the CPU cost of the downgraded codec, and neither document restates the other's half. Required documents: qrv-guide-compression and qrv-incident-2026-08-compression.

text: where does compression happen in the batch path and what warning was added after August 2026
design_note: Joining entity: CodecNegotiator. The guide supplies the position in the batch path; the postmortem supplies the warning, and neither document restates the other's half. Required documents: qrv-guide-compression and qrv-incident-2026-08-compression.

text: what happens when a tenant reaches its quota limit and why did the November 2026 rejections persist after pipeline limits were raised
design_note: Joining entity: TenantQuota. The guide supplies the block-then-reject behaviour and the two limit scopes; the postmortem supplies why raising the per-pipeline limit did not help, and neither document restates the other's half. Required documents: qrv-guide-quotas and qrv-incident-2026-11-quota.

text: when is tenant quota consumption released and what warning was added after November 2026
design_note: Joining entity: TenantQuota. The guide supplies when quota is released; the postmortem supplies the concentration warning, and neither document restates the other's half. Required documents: qrv-guide-quotas and qrv-incident-2026-11-quota.

text: how long are audit entries retained and what must verification tools accept from December 2026
design_note: Joining entity: AuditTrail. The guide supplies the retention period; the advisory supplies the dual-format verification rule, and neither document restates the other's half. Required documents: qrv-guide-audit-log and qrv-security-advisory-audit.

text: what fields does an audit entry carry and how did the audit digest change in December 2026
design_note: Joining entity: AuditTrail. The guide supplies the entry fields; the advisory supplies the digest change, and neither document restates the other's half. Required documents: qrv-guide-audit-log and qrv-security-advisory-audit.

text: what traffic step and hold time does the cutover controller use and why did the September 2026 cutover oscillate
design_note: Joining entity: CutoverController. The guide supplies step and hold; the postmortem supplies why the loop continued, and neither document restates the other's half. Required documents: qrv-guide-cutover and qrv-incident-2026-09-cutover.

text: what triggers an automatic cutover rollback and what changed after September 2026
design_note: Joining entity: CutoverController. The guide supplies the rollback trigger; the postmortem supplies the added conditions, and neither document restates the other's half. Required documents: qrv-guide-cutover and qrv-incident-2026-09-cutover.

text: how does a backfill plan split a date range and how did the March 2026 backfill write duplicates
design_note: Joining entity: BackfillPlan. The guide supplies the segmentation (a managed plan never runs ephemeral, unlike an ad-hoc backfill); the postmortem supplies the two causes of duplication, and neither document restates the other's half. Required documents: qrv-guide-backfill and qrv-incident-2026-03-backfill.

text: what makes a backfill plan refuse to start and what changed after March 2026
design_note: Joining entity: BackfillPlan. The guide supplies the overlap refusal (a managed plan never runs ephemeral, unlike an ad-hoc backfill); the postmortem supplies the fix, and neither document restates the other's half. Required documents: qrv-guide-backfill and qrv-incident-2026-03-backfill.
